title: Convert a `String` date "2020-01-15" to `LocalDate` and calculate the employee's tenure in years.
shortTitle: Convert a String date "2020-01-15" to LocalDate and calculate the employee's tenure in years
keyPoints: LocalDate.parse("2020-01-15") parses an ISO-8601 date string without a custom formatter
ChronoUnit.YEARS.between(joinDate, now) returns completed years, accounting for whether the anniversary has passed
Period.between(join, now).getYears() gives the same completed years as the year component
LocalDate is zone-free; inject a Clock for testable, deterministic 'now'
Catch DateTimeParseException for malformed date strings in production data
Use java.time instead of legacy Date/Calendar to avoid timezone and mutability bugs

s1_definition.oneliner: LocalDate.parse("2020-01-15") creates a date, and ChronoUnit.YEARS.between(join, now) gives completed tenure years.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **LocalDate.parse(text)** parses an ISO-8601 date string (yyyy-MM-dd) into a `LocalDate`.
- **ChronoUnit.YEARS.between(start, end)** returns completed years elapsed.
- **Period.between(start, end).getYears()** gives the years component of a year-month-day breakdown.
- **LocalDate** is zone-free and immutable.
- **Clock injection** makes `LocalDate.now(clock)` deterministic in tests.
s1_definition.analogy: Priya at the National Bank of India reads a joining date written as text, turns it into a real calendar date, and counts how many full years the employee has worked since then.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  String "2020-01-15"
       │
       │  LocalDate.parse()
       ▼
  LocalDate: 2020-01-15
       │
       │  ChronoUnit.YEARS.between(join, now)
       │  now = 2025-01-15
       ▼
  long: 5  (five completed years)

  Note: if now were 2025-01-14 (one day before anniversary)
  → result would be 4 (anniversary not yet passed this year)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To convert a date string to a date and compute tenure, use LocalDate.parse for ISO-format strings and ChronoUnit.YEARS.between for completed years. The java.time API correctly handles the anniversary: if today is before the anniversary, it reports one fewer year.

Inject a Clock so 'now' is deterministic in tests, and catch DateTimeParseException for malformed input. At the National Bank of India, this drives loyalty benefits based on completed years of service.

Always use java.time instead of legacy Date and Calendar. The modern API is immutable, thread-safe, and handles leap years correctly.

Remember one sentence: LocalDate.parse converts a date string, ChronoUnit.YEARS.between gives completed tenure years, and inject a Clock for testable date logic.
